gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-roboto-serif: Wide-set letters with big open eyes and a faint charcoal-like shading make this body text easy to settle into. Roboto Serif sits under Aaargh, whose curves and straights hold one line width, so the page moves from blunt to softly worn.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-sahitya: Sahitya is a bookish text serif whose thin strokes barely trail the thick ones, leaving the s and c mouths uncrowded. Under Aaargh, with its crossbars as fat as the stems, Sahitya's shifting weight feels like a gentle step down.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-sawarabi-mincho: Soft, ink-like modulation and terminals cut well short of the bowl give this serif a refined, hand-drawn feel. Sawarabi Mincho handles the quiet reading, while Aaargh, free of any thick-thin flicker, does the loud, forceful part.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-sedan: Aaargh looks like glass tubing bent into letters, with that generous opening into every e. Sedan's mellow strokes give it a bookish counterweight.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-sedan-sc: Broad open counters and mild thicks make this text serif feel literary and unhurried. Sedan SC keeps its g lightly thinned at the links with sturdy bowls, so extended reading never tires beneath the single-weight outline feel of Aaargh.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-shippori-mincho: Marker-drawn and muscular, then a literary hush. Shippori Mincho supplies the strongest quality here: a classic serif whose gently varied strokes and generous curves soften what Aaargh's one-marker letters shout.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-stix-two-text: STIX Two Text is an editorial serif with thins only slightly lighter than its thicks and terminals pulled back from the curves. STIX Two Text moderates strokes that Aaargh holds as constant as bent wire, so the two feel purposefully different.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-tai-heritage-pro: Aaargh's strokes hold one unvarying weight from word to word, with a generous entry into each e. Make it small and that strength fades; Tai Heritage Pro's gentle taper wouldn't suffer.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-taviraj: Tubing-smooth strength, then bookish restraint. Aaargh is best at blunt, commanding statements cut from one gauge, while Taviraj, a classic serif with medium contrast and generous curve endings, does its best work in steady, quiet reading.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-trirong: Trirong reads like a dip pen used gently, its text serif strokes softly varied and the flared curve ends kept apart. And Aaargh, with thickness that stays put around every curve, gives the page a firm, commanding top.
